zh: 所选数字必须保持原顺序，最多 3 位。可以按“已经处理到的前缀”和“恰好选了几位”来划分状态。
令 best[k] 为当前前缀中恰好选 k 位能组成的最大值。读到新数字 d 时，要么不用它，要么让它当最后一位，从 best[k−1]×10+d 转移。
初始 best[0]=0，其余为不可达（如 −1）。每读一个数字，k 从 3 倒序到 1 更新 best[k]=max(best[k], best[k−1]×10+d)，倒序保证同一个数字不会被用两次。最后输出 best[1]、best[2]、best[3] 中的最大值。
en: The chosen digits keep their original order and there are at most 3 of them, so a state can be the processed prefix plus how many digits are chosen.
Let best[k] be the largest value made from exactly k digits of the current prefix. A new digit d is either skipped or used as the last digit, coming from best[k−1]×10+d.

Start with best[0]=0 and the rest unreachable (for example −1). For each digit update k from 3 down to 1: best[k]=max(best[k], best[k−1]×10+d); going downward keeps a digit from being used twice. Print the maximum of best[1], best[2] and best[3].

explanationEn:
## Idea

best[k] stores the largest value that can be formed by choosing exactly k digits from the processed prefix. When digit d is read, update best[k]=max(best[k],best[k−1]×10+d) in decreasing order of k so that no digit is used more than once.

## Why it is correct

Induction on the prefix length. An optimal choice of exactly k digits either does not use the current digit, coming from the old best[k], or ends with it, obtained by appending the digit to the best k−1 digits of the prefix. The two cases are complete and mutually exclusive. The decreasing order guarantees that the state read is the one of the previous prefix. Finally, taking the maximum over the states with 1..3 digits matches "at most three digits".

## Complexity

O(n) time and O(1) extra space apart from the input.
